name: GDPR Art. 32 — Security of processing
description: EU Regulation 2016/679 (GDPR) Article 32 — technical measures appropriate to the risk of processing personal data. This file maps host-hardening rules to the four technical paragraphs of Art. 32(1).

controls.name: Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data
controls.desc: Personal data must be encrypted at rest and in transit using strong, current cryptography. Weak protocols and ciphers must be disabled, certificates must be valid, and full-disk encryption applied to endpoints.

controls.name: Ongoing confidentiality of processing systems
controls.desc: Access controls preserve confidentiality: no extra UID 0, root SSH disabled, RDP NLA enforced, key-based auth, password policies, world-writable files prevented.

controls.name: Ongoing integrity of processing systems
controls.desc: Mandatory access control, ASLR, restricted SUID, anti-malware and audit logging detect or prevent unauthorised modification of personal data and the systems that process it.

controls.name: Ongoing availability and resilience of processing systems
controls.desc: Patches applied, no Known-Exploited / critical / high CVEs outstanding, network boundary controls active, legacy protocols (SMBv1, LLMNR) disabled.

controls.name: Regular testing and assessment
controls.desc: Regular technical testing of security measures: failed-login monitoring, time-synchronized logs for forensic accuracy, automated vulnerability scanning.
